content.value_statement: Understanding how a Retrieval Augmented Generation system moves from raw documents to answerable context is hard to track across scattered files. This skill provides a clear reference for the ingestion, embedding, and Qdrant vector search stages of a RAG pipeline.
actual_capabilities: Describes the document ingestion process, including scanning, MDX cleaning, and text chunking with defined size and overlap.
Explains the embedding step using a named text embedding model.
Documents the Qdrant vector search setup, including collection name, vector size, and cosine similarity.
Outlines prompt engineering and personalization based on user background attributes.
Summarizes an agentic flow that wraps LLM calls in a custom Agent class.
limitations: This is documentation only; it contains no runnable code or scripts.
It describes a specific project setup and does not provide a general-purpose RAG framework.
It assumes the reader already has the referenced Python files and dependencies in place.
It does not include configuration steps for API keys or Qdrant deployment.

output_examples.input: Summarize the stages of the RAG pipeline described in this skill.
output_examples.output: The pipeline has three main stages. First, ingestion scans a documents folder, cleans the text, splits it into chunks, embeds the chunks, and stores them in a Qdrant collection. Second, vector search retrieves relevant chunks using cosine similarity. Third, prompt engineering builds a context-rich prompt and personalizes system instructions based on the user background.

output_examples.input: Explain how documents are ingested, cleaned, and chunked in this pipeline.
output_examples.output: During ingestion the system scans the documents folder, removes MDX frontmatter and import statements, and splits the remaining text into chunks of one thousand characters with a one hundred character overlap. Each chunk is then embedded and upserted into the vector store.

best_practices: Read the ingestion section first, since later stages depend on how chunks are prepared.
Verify that the referenced Python files exist in the codebase before relying on the described behavior.
Keep the collection name and vector size consistent between ingestion and search.
anti_patterns: Treating this documentation as executable code that will run on its own.
Changing the chunk size or embedding model without updating both ingestion and search.
Assuming the pipeline handles API keys or Qdrant deployment, which are out of scope here.

faq.question: What does this skill contain?
faq.answer: It contains reference documentation describing the architecture of a Retrieval Augmented Generation pipeline.

faq.question: Does this skill run any code?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown documentation file and does not execute any code or scripts.

faq.question: Which vector database does the pipeline use?
faq.answer: The pipeline uses Qdrant, storing vectors in a collection named physical_ai_book.

faq.question: What are the chunking settings?
faq.answer: Text is chunked into segments of one thousand characters with a one hundred character overlap.

faq.question: How is retrieval personalized?
faq.answer: System instructions are tailored using the user software background and hardware background attributes.

faq.question: What similarity metric does the vector search use?
faq.answer: The vector search uses cosine similarity with a vector size of seven hundred sixty eight.
